newsitem.title: INDIA: Birla Yamaha sees 96/97 net at some 100 mln rupees.
newsitem.headline: Birla Yamaha sees 96/97 net at some 100 mln rupees.

text.p: Indian diesel generator maker Birla Yamaha Ltd expects to make a net profit of about 100 million rupees in 1996/97, up from 60.4 million in the previous year, a senior company official said on Wednesday.
"This year's results will be announced shortly. We'll be touching a net profit close to 100 million rupees," S. Rajagopalan, vice-president of marketing and sales, told Reuters.
"Turnover this year, we will be able to touch around 900 million rupees," he said. Sales in 1995/96 (April-March) totalled 692.5 million rupees, Rajagopalan said.
"We have further consolidated ourselves. It is a very happy situation," Rajagopalan said.
The firm exported about 35 percent of its production in both 1995/96 and 1996/97, all under the Yamaha brand name, he said.
India's Birla family holds 40 percent of the firm's equity and Japan's Yamaha Motor Co holds 26 percent. The rest is held by financial institutions and the public.
